title: Manuscript Grid — NeurIPS Two-Column Folio
description: A LaTeX-faithful two-column slide modelled on NeurIPS and ICML paper conventions, with justified serif body, centred numbered equations, and an inset results figure — the only ML-result template that treats typographic protocol as a design feature, not a constraint.
philosophy: This template holds that mathematical rigour deserves equal typographic rigour. It borrows its proportions, hierarchy, and whitespace rhythm directly from decades of IEEE and ACM publishing convention, deliberately rejecting decorative gradients and oversized headers in favour of precise serif spacing, correct math italics, and a paper-white ground that prints as crisply as it renders on a projector. It is built for researchers presenting to researchers — an audience that will notice a missing equation number or a ragged-right abstract before they notice a missing logo. Spectacle is noise; the result is the signal.
goodFor: ML conference poster sessions at NeurIPS, ICML, or ICLR
Slides that must reproduce published paper figures and equations verbatim
Department seminar talks where every line of the abstract will be read aloud
Print-ready A0 poster exports that share layout with the digital deck
avoidFor: Executive keynotes requiring high-impact full-bleed visual storytelling
Sales pitches or brand launch announcements to non-technical stakeholders
Dashboards with six or more simultaneous data panels
Audiences unfamiliar with academic two-column paper conventions
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the first page of a NeurIPS proceedings paper rendered at presentation scale — austere, authoritative, and typographically precise. Paper-white ground dominates throughout; the title commands attention through scale and weight contrast alone, not color or decoration. The two-column abstract block below signals intellectual density and rewards a reader who leans in to parse every justified line. Avoid any gradient, shadow, or illustrative element; the only visual accent permitted is the hairline rule separating the masthead from the body columns.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-width centered masthead zone occupies roughly the top third — title on one or two lines, then an authors row, then an affiliations row, each pair separated by a tight internal hairline rule. Below a second dividing rule, two equal-width columns carry the abstract in justified body text, directly mimicking the first page of a submitted manuscript. Outer margins hold approximately 10% breathing room on all four sides with no decorative header band; hierarchy is achieved entirely through size contrast and vertical spacing. A small conference tag or submission identifier anchors the bottom-right footer area.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a page lifted cleanly from printed conference proceedings — dense, composed, and unsentimental. Two-column rhythm alternates between tight justified prose and the visual pause of a displayed equation, giving the layout a measured scholarly cadence. A small inset figure anchors one column with quiet data authority while the opposing column holds structured running text. No gradients, no decorative flourishes beyond a single thin section rule; every element earns its place through typographic convention, not visual spectacle.

examples.layoutNotes: Two equal text columns separated by a narrow internal gutter, sitting inside breathing outer margins of roughly 7% on each side. A section heading (e.g., '3  Method') spans one column width with a single fine rule beneath it; a displayed equation occupies the full column width with its number pinned flush to the column's right edge. A results figure fills one column edge-to-edge with a centered caption in reduced type below; the opposing column carries full-justified body copy in tight line-height. Folio number is set bottom-center outside the text area, with no header band above the columns.
